note: Published LoCoMo numbers, as their sources give them, for setting beside a run of this bench. Category columns keep each source's own names. In locomo10.json the category numbers are 1 multi-hop, 2 temporal, 3 open-domain, 4 single-hop, 5 adversarial (task_eval/evaluation.py's rules; mem0ai/memory-benchmarks CATEGORY_NAMES); the paper lists the five in another order. Read 2026-11-21.

sources.source: Maharana et al., Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents, ACL 2024 (arXiv 2402.17753), Table 2; static/paper/locomo.pdf at snap-research/locomo 3eb6f2c
sources.setup: The model reads the conversation itself (truncated to its window), asked for a short phrase in the conversation's words ('Use DATE of CONVERSATION' added to temporal questions). The paper's own conversations; the README calls locomo10 a subset of the 50 first released, so these rows may not be on the same ten.

sources.source: Chhikara et al., Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory (arXiv 2504.19413v1), Tables 1 and 2
sources.setup: All 10 conversations, categories 1-4; gpt-4o-mini answers from retrieved memories with an answer prompt asking for a short answer; J is gpt-4o-mini with the ACCURACY_PROMPT score.py uses, 10 runs averaged. Both speakers' facts are memories.

sources.source: Vendor pages as read by the industry-benchmarks survey (work/mibo-migration/industry-benchmarks.json, 2026-11-21)
sources.setup: Self-reported, each with its own answerer, answer prompt and judge. mem0's current harness (mem0ai/memory-benchmarks, Apache-2.0) judges with partial credit, a 14-day date tolerance and gold-overriding evidence: far more lenient than the prompt above.

caveats: Penfield Labs' audit (2026-04-08) found 99 of the 1,540 category 1-4 gold answers wrong (6.4%) and the usual gpt-4o-mini judge accepting 62.8% of deliberately vague wrong answers.
Salesforce ConvoMem (arXiv 2511.10523) notes plain file operations reach about 74%.
